This is a thematic statement about builders rather than an inventory: it has no appendix table and no APNs anywhere, and its addresses come from three places — the photograph captions that illustrate the building typologies (ch. 5) and the architectural styles (ch. 8), each of which gives an address with a build year and usually a builder; the builder biographies in ch. 6, which give the offices, sales offices and houses of the merchant builders; and the model-home lists in ch. 7, which are the densest single seam, 39 named model homes with addresses and dates. The builder table on pp. 68-70 gives active years and associated architects by firm but no addresses, so it produced no findings; it is the key to which builder built which house, and is summarised in the dossier. Never candidates, and so not recorded: roughly twenty block-level references that give no street number (Doelger's first tract on the 1400 block of 39th Avenue, the Rousseau 24-house tract on 33rd between Kirkham and Lawton, Galli's Holiday houses on the 2100 block of 45th Avenue, Clausen's two Art Deco houses on the 2100 block of 33rd Avenue, the five model homes given only as '31st at Lawton' or '33rd Avenue at Kirkham', and Doelger's own hillside house on 15th Avenue), and eight addresses that appear solely as a private person's home or in the 1940 census analysis of who bought these houses (2142 31st Avenue, 1539 33rd Avenue, 1591 33rd Avenue, 1594 29th Avenue, 2381 Bryant Street, 183 Oxford Street, 27 Fountain Street, and 1573 34th Avenue in its second appearance as a resident's address — its model-home fact is kept). Where a building fact and a private buyer appear in the same sentence, the building fact is recorded and the buyer is not: that covers the owners named at 2278 29th Avenue, 2218 35th Avenue, 2230 27th Avenue and 2270 33rd Avenue, and the two veterans who bought 1507 and 1511 33rd Avenue from the Veterans' Welfare Board. Builders, architects and named firms are recorded in their building role, and the six merchant builders whose own houses the statement documents by name and date are recorded as such, which the root AGENTS.md privacy limits permit for individuals from the historical record.

notes: The whole 121-page PDF, read end to end. The statement's own subject is the builders, so nearly every address in it carries a builder attribution, a build year, or both — which is what makes a thematic statement with no inventory table yield as much as this one does. Three cautions. First, the numbered avenues are written straight ('1386 15th Avenue'), unlike the Parkside statement's hyphenated Western Neighborhoods house style, but the PDF text layer drops the ordinal suffix in places ('1500 36 Avenue', '1667 32nd') and wraps addresses across lines, so a regex sweep alone misses several; address_as_written keeps whatever the page prints. Second, the Sunset District was platted in 1868 and almost entirely built after 1925, so no address in this batch needs 1909 renumbering conversion — the one exception is 1321 Mason Street, a pre-1906 Nob Hill address, which is inside the 1906 fire line and cannot refer to a standing building. Third, the statement dates 1746 35th Avenue twice, 1941 in the model-home table and 1940 in the Colonial Revival caption; that disagreement is carried on the finding rather than resolved.
